A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PhysFlow and contain complete main text, references, and Appendices A–D. Their text, equations, tables, and figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic and real-world simulation experiments, a 32-participant human evaluation, and additional experiments and ablations in Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains the original simulation experiments, human evaluation, and appendix results, including numerical comparisons and qualitative outcomes.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same reconstruction methods, GPT-4 material initialization, differentiable MPM simulation, and optical-flow-guided parameter optimization. No algorithm or component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same nine synthetic objects, nine real-world scenes, and single-view scenarios with PhysGen and Kling guidance in Appendix C.3.

E2.justification: Synthetic comparisons retain PAC-NeRF and GIC; real-world comparisons retain PhysGaussian, PhysDreamer, and Physics3D. Table 8 retains PhysGen and PhysGaussian as comparators.

E3.justification: The synthetic evaluation setup, forces and durations in Table 7, RE/EPE/ECMS metrics, and 32-participant evaluation of 36 videos using five-point ratings are unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 and Appendix C.4 retain the same loss-function, initialization, material-type, and density analyses. The large-force tests and supplementary qualitative comparisons are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Human-rating distributions and averaging practices are unchanged. Neither version reports additional repeated-run information, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 2–5 and 8–10 retain the same entries and values, including PhysFlow's 3.44/3.53 human ratings and 3.08 real-world ECMS. The figures retain the same qualitative outcomes despite image recompression.

T1.justification: The continuum-mechanics and MPM formulations, optical-flow loss, ECMS definition in Equations 1–4, and material definitions in Appendix A are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about automatic material initialization, optical-flow-guided refinement, flexible inputs, and realistic 4D simulation.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and applicability qualifications are unchanged. Appendix D retains the limitation concerning missing relighting effects, including dynamic shadows and specular highlights.

D1.justification: Appendix B retains the same implementation information, including Warp, RAFT, SAM2Point, and the NVIDIA A800 GPU. Prompts, force specifications, and the code/data access statement and project URL are unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 50 references and research positioning are retained. No cited work or substantive comparison with prior research is added or removed.

P1.justification: v3 reverses the displayed email order, updates the arXiv version stamp, and expands the acknowledgement by adding grant GRF/PolyU 15607922. Scientific prose and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Images in Figures 3 and 5 are recompressed and partly downsampled, reducing fine detail at magnification while preserving their content, captions, and arrangement. The expanded acknowledgement causes minor reference-page reflow; tables and other figures are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The scientific argument, experimental evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations remain unchanged. v3 adds funding attribution and slightly reduces image detail through compression, but the figures remain interpretable and these edits do not materially change overall paper quality.
